A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Omni-Captioner research work, with readable main text, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–F. Their matching organization supports a reliable comparison, including the revised benchmark material.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioner evaluations in Tables 3–4, Omni-Detective experiments in Figure 6 and Table 5, and human-preference alignment analysis in Figure 7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, ablations, and human-preference study, while reporting revised Omni-Cloze outcomes in Tables 4, 13, and 14.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same Omni-Detective tool-calling procedure, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B backbone, and audio alignment followed by joint audio-visual training. The substantive procedural revisions concern evaluation-benchmark curation.

E1.justification: The VGGSound/FineVideo training sources and all captioning and QA evaluation benchmarks are retained. Omni-Cloze still covers the same nine domains, 47 subcategories, and audio, visual, and audio-visual tasks; its changed counts and modality proportions concern evaluation composition.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments in Tables 2–5 and 7–14. Revised Omni-Cloze scores involve the same proprietary and open-source baselines.

E3.justification: The central benchmark's reported construction and composition are substantially revised. Appendix B.1 replaces its description of post-generation question review with professional verification of source descriptions before generation, and lowers minimum visual/audio/AV blanks from 10/10/5 to 8/8/4. Figure 8 changes 2,340 videos and 70,200 blanks to 2,320 and 69,600, average passage length from 375.1 to 444.6 words, and visual share from 43.2% to 52.2%. Section 5.2 and Figure 5 still describe final question validation, leaving the intended validation sequence inconsistent.

E4.justification: Figure 7a updates the accuracy values and fitted relationship supporting the existing human-Elo alignment analysis, while retaining the reported correlation of 0.91. The investigation-budget analysis, cascade ablation, modality-specific alignment plots, and Appendix F case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: The human-preference study still uses 500 caption pairs with the same Elo hyperparameters. Correlation and shaded-band reporting practices remain unchanged; no new repeated-run counts, seed information, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 4, 13, and 14 substantially replace the central Omni-Cloze accuracy and error-rate results across models. Table 4 reports Audio-Captioner at 53.2% instead of 48.6%, and Omni-Captioner at 56.4% instead of 53.5%; the audio lead over Gemini 2.5 Pro narrows from 7.4 to 5.2 points. These accompany a revised benchmark and do not establish same-setting performance gains. v2 also introduces disagreement between Tables 4b and 14 about Omni-Captioner's modality accuracies. External-benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The cloze evaluation definitions and mathematical content are retained. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: Omni-Detective, two captioners, and Omni-Cloze. Claims about benchmark leadership, the detail–hallucination trade-off, and agreement with human preferences retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of caption completeness, hallucination trade-offs, investigation-step saturation, and human alignment are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitation concerning hallucinations that cannot be reliably assessed against the reference details.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the reported resource status from a promised release to an assertion that the pipeline, models, and benchmark are open source, retaining the same repository link. Appendix B.1 specifies professional annotators checking source descriptions against original clips. Training hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, decoding settings, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and positioning relative to earlier research are unchanged. References moving between pages 10 and 11 result from the added acknowledgement.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to Appendix B.1, result descriptions, and the availability statement. v2 also updates the publication header, affiliation and author-role notes, and adds an acknowledgement. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 7a is redrawn with revised points, fit, shaded band, and vertical scale. The acknowledgement and text edits cause limited reflow of references and appendix material. Figure/table inventories and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Reported professional verification of source descriptions and completed resource release could improve reliability and reuse, but their benefits are not established sufficiently to weigh against newly introduced inconsistencies. Unlike v1, v2's Tables 4b and 14 disagree on Omni-Captioner's visual/audio accuracies: 57.0/54.5 versus 54.6/57.0. Appendix B.2 also retains modality averages superseded in Figure 8, and the validation sequence is inconsistently described. Because the benchmark itself changes, higher scores cannot establish improved model quality. The PDFs do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
